html:
In October 1943, warned that the Germans were about to round them up, about 7,000 of Denmark's roughly 7,800 Jews were hidden by their neighbours and taken across the Sound to neutral Sweden in fishing boats.

Germany had occupied Denmark since April 1940 but let its government run the country. When that broke down in August 1943, the deportation of the Jews was ordered. A German official, Georg Duckwitz, leaked the date. Danes from all walks of life hid families and paid fishermen to carry them over, and Sweden announced it would take them in.

Fewer than 500 were caught and sent to the camp at Theresienstadt, and most of them survived. It stands among the few mass rescues of the Holocaust. One of those who fled was the physicist Niels Bohr.
sum: In October 1943, warned that the Germans were about to round them up, about 7,000 of Denmark's roughly 7,800 Jews were hidden by their neighbours and taken across the Sound to neutral Sweden in fishing boats.
